## CONTRACT 1: JOINT VENTURE AGREEMENT (APEX / KENJI VALVE CO., LTD.)
**Effective Date:** April 3, 2017 | **Governing Law:** Delaware

### 1.1 Definition of Change of Control

**Section/Provision:** Article I — Definitions

**Operative Language:**
> "'Change of Control' means, with respect to any Member, the acquisition, directly or indirectly, by any Person or group of Persons acting in concert (other than such Member's existing Affiliates as of the Effective Date), of fifty percent (50%) or more of the issued and outstanding voting equity interests of such Member, whether by purchase, merger, consolidation, recapitalization, reorganization, or otherwise, or any transaction or series of related transactions that results in a change in the power to direct or cause the direction of the management and policies of such Member."

**Analysis:** The 50% threshold is relatively high compared to the Credit Agreement's dual thresholds (50% for mandatory prepayment; 35% for Event of Default). The Merger (Voltan acquiring 100% of Apex) squarely triggers this definition. Note that the carve-out for "existing Affiliates as of the Effective Date" (2017) does not benefit Voltan.

### 1.2 Notice Obligations

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.1 — Notice of Change of Control

**Operative Language:**
> "Each Member shall provide the other Member with written notice of any Change of Control of such Member promptly, and in any event within ten (10) business days, after the execution of any definitive agreement with respect to such Change of Control, and again within five (5) business days following the consummation of such Change of Control. Such notice shall include a reasonably detailed description of the Change of Control transaction, the identity of the acquiring Person or Persons, and the expected or actual date of consummation, as applicable."

**Analysis:** Notice is required at TWO points: (i) within 10 business days of signing a definitive agreement and (ii) within 5 business days of closing. The Merger Agreement was signed March 14, 2025, meaning notice to Kenji was required by approximately March 28, 2025. Failure to provide timely notice is a material risk; confirm whether notice has been delivered.

### 1.3 Change of Control Not Deemed a Transfer

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.2 — Consent Not Required

**Operative Language:**
> "Notwithstanding Article XI, a Change of Control of a Member shall not be deemed a Transfer of such Member's Membership Interest for purposes of Article XI. Accordingly, a Change of Control shall not require the consent of the non-affected Member under Section 11.1. However, a Change of Control shall be subject to the buy-out option set forth in Section 12.3 of this Agreement."

**Analysis:** Favorable for the transaction in that Kenji's consent to the Merger itself is not required. However, the absence of a consent right is offset by a significant buy-out option (see 1.4 below).

### 1.4 Buy-Out Option

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.3(a) — Grant of Buy-Out Option

**Operative Language:**
> "If either Member undergoes a Change of Control (the 'Affected Member'), the other Member (the 'Non-Affected Member') shall have the right, but not the obligation (the 'Buy-Out Option'), to purchase all (but not less than all) of the Affected Member's Membership Interest in the Company. The Non-Affected Member may exercise the Buy-Out Option by delivering written notice to the Affected Member within ninety (90) days following receipt of the notice of consummation of the Change of Control delivered pursuant to Section 12.1."

**Analysis:** Kenji has a 90-day window following receipt of the closing notice to exercise the buy-out option. This is a significant structural risk: Kenji could force Voltan (as Apex's successor) to sell Apex's 55% JV interest post-Merger.

### 1.5 Successor Entity Carve-Out (Safe Harbor)

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.3(b) — Successor Entity Carve-Out

**Operative Language:**
> "Notwithstanding Section 12.3(a), the Buy-Out Option shall not be exercisable by the Non-Affected Member if the following conditions are BOTH satisfied with respect to the successor entity or acquiring Person (the 'Successor Entity') in the Change of Control transaction:
>
> (i) the Successor Entity commits, in writing delivered to the Non-Affected Member within thirty (30) days following consummation of the Change of Control, to maintain the Affected Member's existing senior management team (including, at a minimum, the Affected Member's chief executive officer and chief technology officer) in their respective positions for a period of not less than eighteen (18) months following the consummation of the Change of Control; AND
>
> (ii) the Successor Entity's consolidated annual revenue derived from fluid control products (including, without limitation, valves, actuators, flow meters, and related automation systems), as reported in the Successor Entity's most recent audited annual financial statements as of the date of consummation of the Change of Control, exceeds Five Hundred Million Dollars ($500,000,000).
>
> Both conditions (i) and (ii) above must be satisfied for this Section 12.3(b) carve-out to apply. If either condition is not met, the Buy-Out Option shall remain fully exercisable by the Non-Affected Member in accordance with Section 12.3(a)."

**Analysis — CRITICAL RISK:** This safe harbor requires analysis of both prongs:

- **Prong (ii) — Revenue Threshold:** The Recitals note that Voltan's "flow control division generates consolidated annual revenue of approximately Four Hundred Ten Million Dollars ($410,000,000)." This is BELOW the $500,000,000 threshold required to satisfy Prong (ii). Unless Voltan's audited financials as of closing demonstrate fluid control revenue exceeding $500M (potentially inclusive of Apex's ~$187.4M revenue if consolidated in time), this prong appears unsatisfied. **If Prong (ii) is not met, the carve-out does not apply and Kenji retains the buy-out option regardless of management retention commitments.**

- **Prong (i) — Management Retention:** The written commitment must be delivered to Kenji within 30 days of closing, covering both the CEO (Patricia Langford) and CTO (Dr. Miriam Hesse) for 18 months. However, the Side Letter discloses that Dr. Hesse's single-trigger acceleration right under the Employment Agreement remains unresolved as of the date of the Merger Agreement. If Dr. Hesse exercises her acceleration right and departs, Voltan may be unable to satisfy this prong even if it commits to retaining her.

**Conclusion on Carve-Out:** Based on available data, the Prong (ii) revenue requirement appears unlikely to be satisfied at closing. Voltan's deal team must verify the arithmetic using Voltan's audited financials. If the carve-out does not apply, Kenji holds a live buy-out option for 90 days post-closing.

### 1.6 Buy-Out Price

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.3(c) — Buy-Out Price

**Operative Language:**
> "If the Non-Affected Member exercises the Buy-Out Option pursuant to Section 12.3(a), the purchase price for the Affected Member's entire Membership Interest (the 'Buy-Out Price') shall be equal to four and one-half times (4.5x) the Company's trailing twelve-month EBITDA as of the last day of the Company's most recently completed Fiscal Year preceding the date of the Non-Affected Member's exercise notice (the 'Valuation Date'). For the avoidance of doubt, the Buy-Out Price shall represent the purchase price for the Affected Member's entire Membership Interest, regardless of such Member's percentage Membership Interest. The Buy-Out Price shall be payable in cash at closing in accordance with Section 12.3(d)."

**Analysis:** JV FY2024 EBITDA is stated at approximately $5,100,000. At 4.5x, the Buy-Out Price = **approximately $22,950,000** (for 100% of Apex's 55% JV interest). This is payable in cash within 60 days of Kenji's exercise notice. Note that the multiplier is applied to 100% of the Affected Member's interest regardless of percentage held — this means Kenji pays $22.95M for a 55% stake (implying a full JV enterprise value of approximately $41.7M at this multiple). Voltan's deal team should model the impact of a forced sale of the JV interest and whether JV revenue (~$14.8M attributable to Apex in FY2024) is reflected in deal pricing.

### 1.7 Closing Mechanics

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.3(d) — Closing of Buy-Out

**Operative Language:**
> "The closing of the purchase and sale pursuant to the Buy-Out Option shall occur within sixty (60) days following the date of the Non-Affected Member's exercise notice..."

**Analysis:** 60-day forced closing timeline. Voltan must be prepared to execute a membership interest transfer on compressed timeline if Kenji exercises.

### 1.8 Dispute Resolution on Buy-Out Price

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.3(e)

**Operative Language:**
> "...the Members shall engage an independent nationally recognized accounting firm (other than either Member's regular auditor) mutually agreed upon by the Members (or, failing such agreement within fifteen (15) days, selected by the American Arbitration Association) to determine the Company's EBITDA for the applicable period. The determination of such independent accounting firm shall be final and binding upon the Members. The costs and expenses of such determination shall be borne equally by the Members."

**Analysis:** Standard hockey-stick dispute mechanism. Note 15-day window to agree on firm before AAA-appointed selection.

### 1.9 Continuing Obligations of Successor

**Section/Provision:** Section 12.4 — Continuing Obligations Following Change of Control

**Operative Language:**
> "(a) all obligations of such Member under this Agreement shall remain in full force and effect and shall be binding upon the Successor Entity;
> (b) the Successor Entity shall, within thirty (30) days following consummation of the Change of Control, execute a joinder agreement in form and substance reasonably satisfactory to the Non-Affected Member, agreeing to be bound by all terms and conditions of this Agreement; and
> (c) the Affected Member shall use commercially reasonable efforts to ensure that the Successor Entity cooperates with the Company and the Non-Affected Member..."

**Analysis:** Voltan must execute a joinder agreement within 30 days of closing. This is an independent obligation separate from the carve-out analysis and must be satisfied regardless of whether Kenji exercises the buy-out option.

### 1.10 Exclusivity Obligation

**Section/Provision:** Section 7.2 — Exclusivity

**Operative Language:**
> "During the term of this Agreement, neither Member shall, directly or through any Affiliate, develop, manufacture, or sell products that are substantially similar to the products manufactured by the Company within the agreed territory (the Asia-Pacific region), except through the Company, without the prior written consent of the other Member."

**Analysis:** Post-Merger, Voltan (as Apex's controlling shareholder) becomes bound by this exclusivity restriction in Asia-Pacific through the Affiliate definition. If Voltan's existing operations include fluid control products sold in Asia-Pacific outside of the JV, this creates an immediate conflict requiring consent from Kenji or restructuring.

### 1.11 Reserved Matters (Board Veto Rights)

**Section/Provision:** Section 6.3 — Reserved Matters

**Operative Language:**
> "Notwithstanding anything to the contrary in this Agreement, the following actions shall require the unanimous approval of all five (5) Managers [including Kenji's 2 managers]..."

**Analysis:** Kenji retains board-level veto rights over major JV decisions regardless of the change of control. This is not a change-of-control provision per se but is material context for post-Merger governance.

### Risk Summary — JV Agreement

| Risk | Severity | Likelihood |
|------|----------|------------|
| Buy-out option exercisable (Prong (ii) revenue threshold likely not met) | HIGH | HIGH |
| $22.95M cash exposure if buy-out exercised | HIGH | HIGH |
| Notice obligation at signing (March 28, 2025 deadline) — confirm delivery | HIGH | MUST CONFIRM |
| Joinder agreement required within 30 days of closing | MEDIUM | CERTAIN |
| Voltan Affiliate exclusivity conflict in Asia-Pacific | MEDIUM | MUST DILIGENCE |
| Dr. Hesse retention risk (Prong (i)) | MEDIUM | MEDIUM |

## CONTRACT 2: CREDIT AGREEMENT (APEX / SUMMIT NATIONAL BANK / RIDGELINE COMMERCIAL CREDIT)
**Effective Date:** September 22, 2022 | **Maturity Date:** September 22, 2027 | **Governing Law:** Ohio

### 2.1 Definition of Change of Control

**Section/Provision:** Section 1.01 — Definitions

**Operative Language:**
> "'Change of Control' shall mean the occurrence of any of the following: (a) any 'person' or 'group' (as such terms are used in Sections 13(d) and 14(d) of the Securities Exchange Act of 1934, as amended) shall acquire, directly or indirectly, beneficial ownership (within the meaning of Rule 13d-3 promulgated by the SEC under said Act) of more than 50% of the outstanding shares of Voting Stock of the Borrower; or (b) the Borrower shall cease to own, directly or indirectly, 100% of the Equity Interests of each of its Subsidiaries (other than Apex-Kenji Precision JV, LLC, in which the Borrower shall at all times maintain an ownership interest of not less than 51%)."

**Analysis:** The Merger (Voltan acquiring 100% of Apex) triggers clause (a). Note also that the JV ownership floor of 51% is embedded here — if Kenji exercises the buy-out option under the JV Agreement and acquires Apex's 55% JV interest, the resulting ownership percentage would drop to 0%, triggering this covenant as well (unless Apex ceases to own the JV interest entirely as a result of the buy-out, which may be separately analyzed as a consent issue). Additionally, Prong (b) creates a cross-dependency with the JV buy-out risk.

### 2.2 Mandatory Prepayment Upon Change of Control

**Section/Provision:** Section 2.09(d) — Change of Control

**Operative Language:**
> "Upon the occurrence of a Change of Control (as defined in Section 1.01), the Borrower shall, within thirty (30) days following such Change of Control, prepay all outstanding Revolving Loans in full, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon, and all Commitments shall automatically terminate. As of the date hereof, the aggregate outstanding Revolving Loans are $42,500,000, and the mandatory prepayment obligation upon the occurrence of a Change of Control (as defined in Section 1.01) shall be equal to the full outstanding principal balance of the Revolving Loans at the time of such Change of Control, together with all accrued and unpaid interest thereon and any other amounts then due hereunder. The Borrower shall deliver written notice to the Administrative Agent of the occurrence of a Change of Control promptly, and in any event within five (5) Business Days, following the date on which the Borrower becomes aware of such occurrence."

**Analysis — CRITICAL RISK:** The Merger triggers mandatory prepayment of all outstanding revolving loans (currently $42,500,000 as of execution, plus accrued interest). This must be addressed at closing. Voltan's financing team must ensure payoff funds are available. Notice to Administrative Agent required within 5 Business Days of awareness of the Change of Control. Commitments automatically terminate — this credit facility will not survive the Merger.

### 2.3 Change in Control as Event of Default (Separate/Lower Threshold)

**Section/Provision:** Section 8.01(j) — Change in Control

**Operative Language:**
> "A 'Change in Control' shall constitute an Event of Default. For purposes of this Section 8.01(j), a 'Change in Control' shall mean (x) the acquisition by any person or group of persons acting in concert of beneficial ownership of more than 35% of the outstanding Voting Stock of the Borrower, or (y) individuals who, as of the Effective Date, constituted the Board of Directors of the Borrower (together with any replacement directors whose election or nomination for election was approved by a vote of a majority of the directors then still in office who either were directors as of the Effective Date or whose election or nomination was previously so approved) ceasing to constitute a majority of the Board of Directors of the Borrower."

**Analysis — CRITICAL RISK:** Note the DUAL TRIGGER structure:
- **"Change of Control"** (Section 1.01): >50% acquisition → mandatory prepayment under Section 2.09(d)
- **"Change in Control"** (Section 8.01(j)): >35% acquisition OR board composition change → Event of Default

The Merger triggers BOTH definitions. As an Event of Default, the lenders may accelerate all Obligations and terminate Commitments (Section 8.02(a)). The mandatory prepayment obligation under Section 2.09(d) (30-day window) is more favorable than the Event of Default remedy (immediate acceleration possible upon direction by Required Lenders), so practical resolution is to prepay within the 30-day window before lenders exercise acceleration remedies.

**CRITICAL NOTE:** Section 10.02(e) requires the written consent of EACH Lender (not just Required Lenders) to amend the Change of Control or Change in Control definitions or Sections 2.09(d)/8.01(j). This means Voltan cannot negotiate a waiver with just the majority lenders — all lenders must consent. Given that there are only two lenders (Summit National Bank and Ridgeline), this is manageable but requires bilateral consent.

**Operative Language (Section 10.02(e)):**
> "amend the definition of 'Change of Control' set forth in Section 1.01 or the definition of 'Change in Control' (as defined in Section 8.01(j)), or amend Section 2.09(d) or Section 8.01(j), in each case without the written consent of each Lender."

### 2.4 Notice of Change of Control

**Section/Provision:** Section 5.07(c)

**Operative Language:**
> "Promptly, and in any event within five (5) Business Days after a Responsible Officer of the Borrower obtains knowledge thereof, deliver to the Administrative Agent written notice of: ...(c) any Change of Control or Change in Control (as those terms are defined herein)..."

**Analysis:** Independent 5-Business-Day notice obligation consistent with Section 2.09(d).

### 2.5 JV Ownership Covenant

**Section/Provision:** Section 1.01 — Definition of "Change of Control" clause (b)

**Operative Language:**
> "...the Borrower shall cease to own, directly or indirectly, 100% of the Equity Interests of each of its Subsidiaries (other than Apex-Kenji Precision JV, LLC, in which the Borrower shall at all times maintain an ownership interest of not less than 51%)."

**Analysis:** If Kenji exercises the JV buy-out option and Apex sells its 55% JV interest, Apex would own 0% of the JV. This is below the 51% floor and could constitute an additional independent Change of Control event under the Credit Agreement. However, the credit facility will presumably be repaid in full at closing of the Merger, rendering this moot if prepayment is executed promptly.

### 2.6 Material Contract Cross-Default

**Section/Provision:** Section 8.01(k) — Material Contract Termination

**Operative Language:**
> "The termination, rescission, or material breach of any Material Contract (as listed on Schedule 3.08 or subsequently notified to the Administrative Agent), if such termination, rescission, or material breach would reasonably be expected to result in a Material Adverse Effect."

**Analysis:** Cascading risk: If the Merger triggers termination of any Material Contract (e.g., the Northland MSA or PacWest Agreement), that termination could independently constitute an Event of Default under the Credit Agreement (if Material Adverse Effect threshold is met). This underscores the importance of analyzing each Material Contract.

### Risk Summary — Credit Agreement

| Risk | Severity | Likelihood |
|------|----------|------------|
| Mandatory prepayment of $42.5M+ revolving loans within 30 days of closing | CRITICAL | CERTAIN |
| Event of Default triggered by >35% acquisition (board change at Merger) | CRITICAL | CERTAIN |
| All-lender consent required to amend CoC/CiC provisions | HIGH | N/A (repay instead) |
| 5-Business-Day notice obligation to Administrative Agent | HIGH | CERTAIN |
| JV 51% floor creates cross-exposure if buy-out exercised | MEDIUM | CONTINGENT |

## CONTRACT 3: TECHNOLOGY LICENSE AGREEMENT (APEX / HENDRICKS AUTOMATION SYSTEMS)
**Effective Date:** March 1, 2020 | **Agreement No.:** HAS-LIC-2020-0088 | **Term:** Through February 28, 2030

### 3.1 Definition of Change of Control

**Section/Provision:** Section 1.3 — Definitions

**Operative Language:**
> "'Change of Control' means, with respect to Licensee, (a) any merger, consolidation, or reorganization involving Licensee, whether or not Licensee is the surviving entity; (b) the sale, transfer, or other disposition of all or substantially all of Licensee's assets; (c) the acquisition by any person or group of persons of beneficial ownership of more than fifty percent (50%) of the outstanding voting securities of Licensee; or (d) any other transaction or series of related transactions that results in a change in the identity of the person or persons who ultimately control Licensee. For purposes of clarity, a Change of Control shall be deemed to have occurred regardless of the form of transaction, including without limitation forward mergers, reverse mergers, triangular mergers, and any combination thereof."

**Analysis:** Exceptionally broad definition, explicitly covering triangular mergers (the Merger is structured as a forward triangular merger with Merger Sub merging into Apex). The "regardless of form" language eliminates any structural workaround.

**IMPORTANT NOTE:** The License Agreement does NOT contain an express termination right or consent requirement triggered by a Change of Control in the contract text provided. The agreement contains a change-of-control definition but the operative consequences must be confirmed by reviewing Article 9 (Termination) in full.

### 3.2 Non-Transferability of License

**Section/Provision:** Section 2.1 — License Grant

**Operative Language:**
> "This license is personal to Licensee and may not be transferred, sublicensed, or assigned except as expressly permitted herein."

**Analysis — HIGH RISK:** The license is explicitly non-transferable. The Merger technically results in Apex surviving as a wholly-owned subsidiary of Voltan, so there is a question of whether the license has been "transferred" (arguably not, since Apex remains the contracting entity). However, if the Merger is treated as a change of entity identity or if any subsequent integration steps assign or novate the license, Hendricks' consent will be required. Additionally, if the broad Change of Control definition in Section 1.3 connects to any termination or consent right in Article 9 (not reproduced in the data room documents), this could be a critical gap.

**DATA ROOM GAP:** Article 9 (Termination provisions of the License Agreement) was not included in the provided document excerpts. The consequence of a Change of Control under the License Agreement is not determinable from the available text. **This is a critical diligence gap that must be addressed before closing.**

### 3.3 Revenue Context

The FlowLogic algorithm is embedded in the AX-7000 Product Line, which generates approximately **$52.3 million in trailing twelve-month revenue** (per Credit Agreement Schedule 3.08). Loss of this license or disruption to its terms would be material.

### 3.4 Derivative Works / IP Ownership

**Section/Provision:** Section 2.4 and Section 5.2

**Operative Language:**
> "Any Derivative Works created by Licensee with Licensor's prior written consent shall be owned exclusively by Licensor, and Licensee hereby assigns all right, title, and interest in such Derivative Works to Licensor."

> "Any improvements, modifications, enhancements, or Derivative Works of the Licensed Technology developed by Licensee, whether with or without Licensor's consent, shall be owned exclusively by Licensor."

**Analysis:** All improvements to FlowLogic, even those developed by Apex without Hendricks' consent, are automatically assigned to Hendricks. Voltan's deal team should investigate the extent of Apex's R&D contributions to FlowLogic functionality and whether Apex has clean IP ownership in the AX-7000 platform separable from FlowLogic enhancements.

### Risk Summary — License Agreement

| Risk | Severity | Likelihood |
|------|----------|------------|
| Termination/consent right upon Change of Control (Article 9 not reviewed) | CRITICAL | UNKNOWN — DILIGENCE GAP |
| Non-transferability of $52.3M revenue-generating license | HIGH | MUST CONFIRM |
| Derivative works ownership risk | MEDIUM | ONGOING |
